deck: This week, capital continues to flow while delays and partnerships shape the landscape.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amidst co-orbital concerns
stories.body: True Anomaly has secured a $190 million Series C funding round, boosting its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and satellite data awareness, aligning well with increasing DoD interests in space resilience. With this capital, True Anomaly is well-positioned to enhance its offerings in an increasingly crowded market.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where cash often trumps innovation, True Anomaly's funding reflects a growing appetite for security solutions in orbit, even if their tech is still in the proving stage.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris join forces for SDA
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris have teamed up to bid on a tactical Space Development Agency constellation project, showcasing the importance of partnerships in the defense space. The collaboration comes at a time when the SDA is ramping up its efforts to enhance space-based capabilities, aiming for a more integrated approach to national security.
stories.soWhat: As competition heats up, this partnership highlights a strategic pivot; in space, collaboration can often be more valuable than individual prowess, especially when the stakes are high.

stories.head: Boeing demonstrates quantum protocol for 2027 launch
stories.body: Boeing has successfully demonstrated a quantum networking protocol in preparation for a planned 2027 launch. While this may sound like the stuff of science fiction, the implications for secure communications in space are significant, especially as more satellites enter orbit. Boeing's push into quantum tech may position it ahead in the race for secure satellite communications.
stories.soWhat: If Boeing can deliver on this promise, they might just redefine secure communications in a sector that desperately needs it, though the timeline remains a question mark.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Spark Space's engine tests
watchlist.body: With Spark Space's recent engine tests and funding, their progress could disrupt the electric rocket market if they deliver on their claims.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant progresses
watchlist.body: As Sierra Space's Dream Chaser clears its design review, the focus will shift to whether it can meet the rigorous demands of DoD contracts.

watchlist.title: Anticipate more on satellite servicing economy
watchlist.body: The FCC's satellite authorizations could lead to a surge in the satellite servicing economy, especially as companies look to carbon credits for inspiration.

watchlist.title: Watch for further delays in hypersonic tests
watchlist.body: With hypersonic glide-vehicle tests slipping again, expect more scrutiny on the technology's viability and the implications for defense strategies.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
